body: All coverage was taken with a low-quality camera, often called "Shitcam". The car is completely blurred, with a large blur at the back and a smaller one at the front. This newer variant is dimmer and hazier, also found in Nigeria.
Portuguese is the main language of São Tomé and Príncipe.
Portuguese influence is visible in the infrastructure, including ladder poles and pedestrian signs identical to those in Portugal.
São Tomé and Príncipe are tropical islands covered in rainforests, with banana plants being very common.
Some wooden poles are painted blue at the bottom and may have the letters "CST" on them.
A desaturated and dimmer "shitcam" variant is most common on the island of Príncipe.
Oil palm plantations can be found in the southern part of São Tomé.
In the town of Trindade, utility poles are painted with red and white stripes.
